findings.text: Boot initialization completes immediately when the feature flag is off and otherwise delegates to one time setup that allocates caches workqueue shrinker and fallback pool.

Lifecycle uses uninitialized succeeded and failed states. Uninitialized permits recording parameters or running first setup. Succeeded permits runtime reconfiguration. Failed forbids use. Setup transitions from uninitialized to succeeded on full or degraded success and to failed when early resource acquisition fails.

Compressor change while running reuses a decommissioned pool with the requested name when available and otherwise builds a fresh pool. Reused pools have their reference revived before installation. Success installs the chosen pool at the head of the global collection and marks availability. Failure leaves current selection unchanged and stages the candidate for release. Release of the replaced pool is signaled after protection is dropped.

Enabled flag handling records only the boolean before the system is running. After boot it runs one time setup if still uninitialized then requires a configured pool before accepting enablement and rejects changes when initialization has failed.

One time setup acquires entry cache processor preparation state unbound reclaim workqueue shrinker memcg aware list background work and fallback pool in order then initializes observability and marks success. Fallback absence disables the feature yet still reports success. Any earlier failure unwinds acquired resources in reverse marks failure disables the feature and reports memory exhaustion.

Per processor preparation returns early when the context already holds a compression handle which makes repeated offline online cycles safe. Otherwise it obtains a page sized node local buffer plus a node local compression handle and request for the pool algorithm initializes completion waiting and mutual exclusion and wires a backlog tolerant completion callback. Allocation failure releases partial context and reports memory exhaustion.

Writeback allocates a locked swap cache folio under current policy after briefly pinning the swap device then validates that the swap slot still points at the same compressed record before dereferencing it. On match it decompresses into the folio erases the slot accounts the event globally and per owner when present frees the record marks the folio current and reclaim preferred and submits it for input output. Allocation mismatch or decompression failure discards the folio path without altering the tree.

Least recently used walk grants a second opportunity to marked entries by clearing the mark and rotating them. Unmarked entries are moved to the tail while protected then released and written back using only a stack copy of the swap slot. Success advances the written counter and failure advances the reclaim failure counter. Observing a page already in swap cache can stop the walk to preserve hotter entries.

Reclaim accounting reports no work when disabled when the owning group forbids writeback when the reclaim context lacks filesystem input output permission or when stored or reclaimable counts are empty. Otherwise it atomically consumes recent disk swapin counts against reclaimable size to reserve protection then scales the remainder by backing to stored ratio so stronger compression evicts less.

Background work reclaims until total compressed pages reach an acceptance threshold. It visits online memory groups in round robin order through a persistent cursor skipping groups without eligible pages or with writeback disabled and yields between groups. A full pass without candidates or repeated failures aborts after a bounded retry count.

Observability provides read only counters for pool limit hits rejection causes decompression failures and written pages plus computed values for total byte size stored pages and incompressible stored pages. Directory creation fails when debug infrastructure is unavailable. An alternate build offers a no operation initializer that always succeeds.

Initialization state inspection and parameter recording are serialized by a dedicated initialization mutex. The mutex is released before availability checks pool creation and reference teardown signaling that may block.
Global pool collection lookup detachment and insertion hold bottom half disabling spin protection. Pool creation parameter recording and teardown signaling run outside that protection.

Per group list protection covers mark inspection and tail rotation and is released before writeback input output. Tail move before release lets concurrent invalidation unlink safely and leaves failures at the back.

Global shrink cursor advancement to the next online group holds dedicated shrink spin protection while retaining an extra online reference. Group shrinking threshold checks and yielding run without that protection.

A pool links global membership hotplug membership per processor contexts reference counting and an algorithm name. An entry links list membership a swap slot a referenced mark and optional ownership accounting. A per processor context holds a page buffer a compression handle a request a wait state and mutual exclusion.

Releasing list protection before writeback allows concurrent invalidation to free the entry. Correctness depends on copying the swap slot to the stack before release and dereferencing only after the tree slot is confirmed to still hold the same pointer while folio locking secures the slot.

Failed or redundant pool candidates must not replace the current pool. They are staged at the tail of the collection so later release processing can destroy them when empty while successful paths replace membership and retire the old pool.
Reclaim identity uses name mm-zswap with NUMA awareness and memcg awareness zero batch and default seek cost.

Debug directory is zswap with read only counters pool_limit_hit reject_reclaim_fail reject_alloc_fail reject_kmemcache_fail reject_compress_fail reject_compress_poor decompress_fail written_back_pages.
Computed debug entries are pool_total_size stored_pages stored_incompressible_pages reporting total bytes stored count and incompressible stored count.
